name: Rabbit

app.note: The app puts the standing shoulder joints 0.8513179 m above the floor (ANIMALS of tools/studio-body.ts). The scale is 1.467789 m for each unit: 1.2 times the scale that put the shoulder joints at 0.581 m, the shoulder joints of the parametric rabbit, because the user asked for a rabbit 1.2 times the size on 2026-10-14 (docs/research/2026-10-14-animal-size.md). The leg factor raises the shoulder joints from 0.475 to 0.58 units, and the scale stays, so that the trunk, the head, and the arms keep their meters (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form.md). The user asked for a full violin on 2026-10-14 ("fox and rabbit violin too small"), and the arms reached 0.5574 m (docs/research/2026-10-14-neck-violin.md). Then the user asked for shorter arms with the same violin ("reduce the arm length of the fox and rabbit without changing the violin size"). Of the reaches 0.4523 m, 0.5056 m, and 0.5574 m, the manager chose the middle one, so the reach is 0.5056 m, and the violin stays 0.958 of the violin of the app (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest.md).

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm that gives the reach of app.reach from the joints below at the scale of app.shoulders. pnpm rig-mesh prints the reach and stops when it is more than 1% from app.reach. The factor was 1.445 before the full violin and 1.81 with it, and the middle factor 1.63 shortens the arms that the user found too long (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest.md).
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises 0.105 units, so that the soles stay at y 0. The user asked for longer legs and a higher seat on 2026-10-14, and then said that the legs of the factor 2.5 were too long. The legs gave a seat of 0.215 m, 0.67 H (0.123 m before). Since 2026-10-16, the chair of the app fits the legs (no seat of ANIMALS), so the soles stand on the floor, and the slanted shins and the flat feet give a seat of 0.136 m (docs/research/2026-10-16-seat-rest/). The factor 2.75 gave the seat of the reference rabbit (1.03 H against 1.07 H), with standing animals that were too tall (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-form.md).
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-13-rabbit-mesh/. sections.py gives the cuts at each height: the feet and the legs below y 0.13, the body from 0.13 to 0.53 with the narrow neck at 0.53, the head from 0.55, and the ear bases at 0.765 (the middle of the ear cut at 0.77). The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut, as in the studio rabbit. The leg joints lie on the middle of the leg cuts, the ankle at the narrow cut 0.05 above the soles, and the toes at the ball of the foot. The cuts at x 0.106 to 0.226 give the middle line of the free arm. The shoulder joint lies on that line, 0.03 inside the root of the arm. The elbow lies halfway to the wrist and 0.01 behind the line. The wrist lies where the paw starts, and the finger joint at the claws. The tail joint lies at the front of the tail ball, whose middle the cuts at z -0.185 to -0.145 give. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The arm bones take the normal of the palm (palm): inward and back, across the paw.

studio.note: The seat of a long thigh, made with docs/research/2026-10-16-seat-rest/leg_turns.py: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The thigh lies level on the seat, 8 degrees out, so that the haunch and the back of the thigh rest on the seat (the user saw the rabbit sitting on the edge of the chair on 2026-10-14). The shin slants 23.8 degrees forward of vertical (the shin of the source slants 20 degrees back), so that the knee angle from the side is 113.8 degrees, as the knee of the red fox (tools/mesh-rigs/fox.json), and the feet stand in front of the knees (90 degrees before). The foot and the toes keep the turn of the source, so that the soles stand flat on the floor. The seat of the studio rabbit (a thigh turn of 57 degrees) left the longer thighs slanted down, with the knees low in front of the chair. The bind arms are the bind arms of the studio rabbit (lowpoly-studio/animals/rabbit/out/rabbit.glb), from docs/research/2026-10-13-rabbit-mesh/studio-targets.ts: the unit direction of each left arm bone in the bind pose.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units). A longer thin face spans a joint, and one set of weights there pulls the side of the trunk out with the arm.

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends. Lower angles turned over more faces of the arms (pnpm fold-probe violinist).

weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). Bone heat gave the top of each shoulder up to 0.18 of the head weight, and the turns of the head pulled it.
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest. With the full share, the curl of the fingers in the app turned over one face between the hand and the fingers of each paw in each play sample (pnpm fold-probe violinist).

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the haunch stays on the seat and only the leg below it turns.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts of sections.py x show the arm apart from the body from x 0.106 out. Inside that plane, the shoulder follows the upper arm and no lower bone of the arm. Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only: the eyes, the nose, and the whiskers. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail ball follows the tail only: the vertices near its middle and behind the plane z = behind, where the cuts of sections.py z show the ball apart from the body (z -0.145).

refine.ringsNote: Each ring cuts the edges of an arm near a joint with the plane through the joint, at right angles to the mean direction of the bone before the joint and the bone after it: joint (the arm bone that starts at the joint), radius (units from the joint), minEdge (the shortest edge that the ring cuts, in units), ends (the smallest part of the edge from each corner), and sides (L, R, or LR, both by default). A new vertex takes the place, the UV, and the weights of its place on the edge, and each split face takes its color from the texture again. With no rings, the faces of the source stay. The rabbit has a ring at each elbow: faces of the source run from the shoulder over the elbow to the forearm, and the bend of the bind pose made them thin, so that they folded in 45% of the play samples (pnpm fold-probe violinist). With the arm factor 1.81 of 2026-10-14, the corners of these faces lie beyond 0.1 units from the elbow, the faces of both elbows folded in each sample, and the rings of 0.13 units on both sides folded the rabbit in 2.5% of the play samples. With the arm factor 1.63, a thin face of the left elbow that the ring left whole (an edge shorter than 0.08 units) folded in 49.6% of the play samples, at each radius from 0.115 to 0.14 units. The rings cut the edges from 0.06 units, and the rabbit folds in 0.9% of the play samples with the hold of main (docs/research/2026-10-14-arms-rest/rig-mesh-check-rabbit-fold.log). Before, with shorter arms, a ring at the right elbow pulled the inner elbow 1.8 cm into the trunk when the bow arm hung. A ring at each shoulder put more folded faces on the top of the right shoulder.

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind mesh flips to the corner of the face on its other side. The two faces must lie almost on one plane in the source and in the bind mesh (normals within normals, in degrees), and the flip must move the surface by at most move (units) in both. The flips run in rounds until no edge flips. The angle 180 turns the flips off. The move of 0.0016 units is 2 mm in the app.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind mesh with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings). The values are the sliver angle and the minEdge and the radius of the ring at the left elbow.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at the samples of a grid of the given steps on the face. A face is dark when its share of samples with a linear luminance below dark is at least eyeShare, and then it takes the mean of its dark samples. Each other face takes the mean of its samples that are not dark, so that the black gaps between the islands of the texture do not darken it. A dark face in the eye box (the left eye, mirrored for the right eye) is a face of an eye. A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color than to white is a face of the nose. Then each face takes the nearest color of a palette of palette colors, from k-means in Oklab, so that the packed mesh of the app holds few colors.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most this number of points of their edge, lifted this far (units) along the normal of the eye, so that the shells keep the triangles within the budget of a studio body. pnpm studio-body finds each eye by its fan, drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The old eye is the dark faces and each face whose middle lies within reach times the radius of their edge, seen along the normal of the eye. After the palette, the faces of the old eye take the color with the largest area in the ring of faces that share a corner with it, so that no outline of the old eye shows around the pea eye. Then each patch of dark faces (the faces that share corners) that no old eye holds, with its middle within darkReach times the radius of the edge and within half the radius of its plane, takes the color with the largest area in the ring of faces that share a corner with the patch. The values of reach and darkReach are the values of the fox.

chair.note: Its front edge lies 0.051 units (7.5 cm) behind the back of the knees of the seated bind (the shins from z 0.103, pnpm rig-mesh prints it), so that no shin lies over the seat, and the haunch (z -0.04 to -0.19) and the thighs sit on it. The chair of the app is 0.03 m deeper at the front (seatBack of ANIMALS), so that its front edge is 4.5 cm behind the back of the knees, as on a real chair. The user said "let the fox and rabbit sit in more" on 2026-10-16. The seat top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat: the thighs near the knees, 0.021 units below the seat top of the chair that ended behind the heels.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind, with the rule of the fox (sit of tools/mesh-rigs/fox.json). The manager found the back of the haunch 2 to 5 cm above the seat on 2026-10-14. The drop is at most 0.03 units, and it fades over the last 0.02 units of the haunch, because the round back of the haunch meets the tail ball there: with no limit, 17 faces between the haunch and the ball turned over. The side view of the underside behind the hip joints, with no part of the last 0.02 units, is 3.7 cm above the seat at most before, and 0.8 cm after (docs/research/2026-10-14-fox-rabbit-fix.md).
